links.outcome: Expert acceptance of context-grounded LLM outputs on oncology report prompts
links.effect: Automatic model selection with context achieved expert acceptance across all 19 prompts; a fixed high-end model had higher cost and lower expert-rated quality. No comparison without context was reported.
links.quote: Evaluated on 19 representative clinical prompts derived from real-world oncology reports, automatic model selection with context achieved expert acceptance across all prompts while reducing inference cost by an order of magnitude; by contrast, a fixed high-end model produced higher cost and lower expert-rated quality.

unlisted_practices: Provider-agnostic model routing that selects an LLM per query by capability and cost profile

screen.reason: The paper empirically evaluates an orchestration framework (OncoGPT) that adds dynamic context grounding/injection and model routing to general off-the-shelf LLMs, comparing outcomes (cost and expert-evaluated quality) against unrouted fixed models.

primary.practice: orchestration layer with context grounding and model routing
